standard.title: Algorithms for factors and divisibility
standard.description: Create and use algorithms involving a sequence of steps and decisions and digital tools to experiment with factors, multiples and divisibility; identify, interpret and describe emerging patterns
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can apply written algorithms involving sequences of steps (AC9M4N09). They have not yet designed algorithms for mathematical investigation or used digital tools to experiment with factors and multiples.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students create and use algorithms to experiment with factors, multiples and divisibility and identify, interpret and describe emerging patterns.

nodes.label: What is an algorithm?
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe an algorithm as a sequence of steps and decisions, and identify algorithms in familiar mathematical procedures.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe a familiar calculation procedure (e.g. checking divisibility by 2) as a sequence of steps; represent it as a written or visual flowchart.
nodes.typical_width: Identify the decision points (if/else) in a mathematical procedure; translate a verbal procedure into a step-by-step algorithm using flowchart notation or pseudocode.
wider: Compare algorithm representations: written steps vs flowchart vs code
Investigate algorithms used in everyday technology (e.g. sorting, searching)

response_modes.reason: The explicit step-decomposition of a procedure is a reasoning scaffold students need before creating their own algorithms. Without this, algorithm creation defaults to vague descriptions rather than precise sequences.

nodes.hinge_reason: Step-decomposition understanding is the prerequisite for Node 2 — students who cannot distinguish steps from decisions cannot create a valid algorithm for testing factors or divisibility.
success_criteria: Student describes a familiar procedure as a sequence of steps
Student identifies at least one decision point in the procedure

nodes.label: Creating algorithms for factors and multiples
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create an algorithm that tests or generates factors, multiples or divisibility for a given number.
nodes.minimum_width: Create a step-by-step algorithm (written or diagrammatic) that tests whether a number is divisible by a given divisor; trace through the algorithm for at least two examples.
nodes.typical_width: Design and trace algorithms for finding factors, listing multiples, or testing divisibility; refine the algorithm based on tracing errors; use digital tools (e.g. spreadsheet formulas or block-based code) to implement and test.
wider: Implement the Sieve of Eratosthenes as an algorithm in a digital tool

response_modes.reason: Algorithm design for different purposes (factors vs multiples vs divisibility) reveals how small changes in the decision logic produce different behaviours. Variety prevents students from memorising one template.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Sieve of Eratosthenes implementation is genuinely rich — combines algorithm design, factor reasoning and digital tool application.
success_criteria: Student creates an algorithm that correctly tests or generates factors/multiples
Student traces the algorithm with specific inputs and gets correct outputs

nodes.label: Identifying patterns
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use their algorithm and digital tool outputs to identify, interpret and describe emerging patterns in factors, multiples and divisibility.
nodes.minimum_width: Run an algorithm on multiple inputs and describe at least one pattern in the results.
nodes.typical_width: Investigate patterns across a range of numbers using digital output; describe patterns using mathematical language (e.g. 'multiples of 6 are always even'); propose and test conjectures about patterns.
wider: Investigate the pattern of factor counts across the first 100 natural numbers
Connect patterns to visual representations: factor rainbows, number grids

response_modes.reason: Pattern identification requires algorithm creation, digital tool use and mathematical vocabulary to work together. The interpretation task — giving meaning to digital output — is the Mode B capability being assessed.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Conjecture-and-test with digital tools is rich, open-ended territory for advancing students.
success_criteria: Student identifies at least one pattern from algorithm output
Student describes the pattern using appropriate mathematical language
